simple: a standard set of library calls that lets many separate programs, often on different computers, send each other data and compute together.
analogy: the delivery rules every kitchen hall in the chain agrees to follow.
precise: a library interface specified by the MPI Forum in "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard"; processes have private memory and exchange data only through explicit calls (point-to-point, collective, one-sided); implementations include Open MPI, MPICH and MVAPICH. The library used here reports MPI API version 3.1.0.
source: D1 of F8-07 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard"); R1 of F8-07 (run of Listing 1 (mpi_basics.log), Open MPI 4.1.6 with g++ 13.3.0, 1, 2 and 4 processes, exit code 0. The MPI API version 3.1.0 is printed by ompi_info on the same machine) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named group of processes that talk to each other; every MPI call says which group it is about.
analogy: the delivery list a parcel is addressed within; the same hall can be on several lists with a different number on each.
precise: an opaque object (MPI_Comm) that combines a group of processes with a communication context, so messages and collectives in one communicator never match those in another; MPI_COMM_WORLD contains all processes started together.
source: D1 of F8-07 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one process sends a message to one other process.
analogy: one labelled parcel from one hall to one other hall.
precise: a send and a receive matched by communicator, source rank and tag; the data are described by (buffer address, count, datatype).
source: D1 of F8-07 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a call that starts a transfer and returns at once; you ask later whether it has finished.
analogy: handing a parcel to the delivery desk and getting a ticket, instead of waiting at the door.
precise: MPI_Isend, MPI_Irecv (and non-blocking collectives such as MPI_Iallreduce) return an MPI_Request; the buffer must not be reused (send) or read (receive) until MPI_Wait/MPI_Test or their "all/some" forms report completion.
source: D1 of F8-07 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each process keeps a copy of the cells at its neighbours' edges and refreshes those copies every step.
analogy: tasting the edge plate of the neighbouring hall's stretch of table.
precise: in a domain decomposition, ghost (halo) cells around each subdomain hold copies of neighbouring subdomains' boundary values; before each stencil update the boundary values are sent to the neighbours and the halos filled from them (milestone F4's "halo-exchange (stencil) example").
source: C1 of F8-07 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14.3, milestone F4 "MPI and GPU-aware MPI": goal, build and acceptance tests, quoted verbatim (a map, not a source, AH-4))

simple: two ways a library delivers a message: small ones are pushed to the receiver straight away; large ones wait until the receiver is ready.
analogy: small parcels left on the doorstep; big ones only handed over when the neighbour opens the door.
precise: implementation protocols, not MPI Standard terms: in an eager send the data travel with the first packet and are buffered at the receiver if no receive is posted; in a rendezvous send a first fragment announces the message and the bulk moves only after the receiver has matched it. Open MPI's per-transport parameter btl_<name>_eager_limit sets the switch-over size ("Maximum size (in bytes, including header) of 'short' messages").
source: D2 of F8-07 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series); R3 of F8-07 (ompi_info --param btl vader|tcp --level 9 on this build (eager_limits.log); the components listed by ompi_info (btl: ofi, openib, tcp, vader, self; coll: sm, tuned, self, monitoring, adapt, sync, libnbc, basic, inter, han) and btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = "cma" were read with the same tool while preparing the chapter) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that finishes no matter how much the library is willing to buffer.
analogy: a delivery plan that works even if no hall ever leaves anything on a doorstep.
precise: the MPI Standard allows a standard-mode MPI_Send to return either after buffering the data or only after a matching receive has started; a program whose completion depends on buffering is called unsafe.
source: D1 of F8-07 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an MPI library that accepts the address of GPU memory in its send and receive calls and moves the data itself.
analogy: the delivery crew that recognises pantry crates and fetches them.
precise: an MPI implementation that detects device pointers passed as buffers (for NVIDIA GPUs through CUDA's unified virtual addressing and pointer-attribute queries) and moves the data with GPU-capable transports: peer copies or inter-process handles inside a node, GPUDirect RDMA or pipelined staging between nodes. Support is a build-time property of the library (and of its transport layer). The MPI Standard itself does not mention GPUs.
source: D2 of F8-08 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series); D5 of F8-08 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); C1 of F8-08 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14.1 rows "MPI with GPUs" and "GPUDirect", and section 14.3 milestone F4 (goal, build, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: copying GPU data into ordinary computer memory, sending that, and copying it back into the other GPU.
analogy: carrying the crate from the pantry to the loading dock and back in at the other end.
precise: a device-to-host copy into a (preferably pinned) host buffer, a host-to-host MPI transfer, and a host-to-device copy at the receiver; done by the application when the library is not GPU-aware, or by the library internally (often in pipelined chunks) when no direct GPU path exists.
source: C1 of F8-08 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14.1 rows "MPI with GPUs" and "GPUDirect", and section 14.3 milestone F4 (goal, build, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source (AH-4)); D2 of F8-08 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: host and GPU memory share one range of addresses, so a pointer alone tells you where the memory is.
analogy: every crate in every room has a unique shelf number, so the crew knows from the number whether it is in the pantry or on the dock.
precise: a CUDA feature in which host and device allocations of a process occupy one virtual address space; cudaPointerGetAttributes returns a cudaPointerAttributes whose type is one of cudaMemoryTypeUnregistered, cudaMemoryTypeHost, cudaMemoryTypeDevice or cudaMemoryTypeManaged (enum in the installed driver_types.h).
source: H2 of F8-08 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed, read in this build: driver_types.h (cudaMemoryTypeUnregistered, cudaMemoryTypeHost, cudaMemoryTypeDevice, cudaMemoryTypeManaged; struct cudaPointerAttributes), cuda_runtime_api.h (cudaPointerGetAttributes; the pageable-copy "staging memory for DMA transfer" note quoted in F1-62's glossary entry), crt/device_double_functions.h (__dadd_rn, __dsub_rn, __dmul_rn, each with the "note_nofma" marker)); D5 of F8-08 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named setting of Open MPI that you can read and change without recompiling.
analogy: a switch on the delivery company's control panel.
precise: a parameter of Open MPI's Modular Component Architecture, set with mpirun --mca <name> <value> or the environment, and listed with its value, source and help text by ompi_info; read-only parameters such as mpi_built_with_cuda_support report how the library was built.
source: D2 of F8-08 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series); R2 of F8-08 (ompi_info and the UCX module folder on this build (ompi_build.log); package versions from the system's package list (UCX 1.16.0)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a communication library that many MPI libraries use underneath to reach the network and the GPUs.
analogy: the company that owns the vans and the road permits, hired by the delivery service.
precise: an open-source communication framework with transports for shared memory, TCP, InfiniBand/RoCE verbs and GPU memory, loaded as modules; Open MPI can use it as its point-to-point layer (this build was configured --with-ucx, R2).
source: D4 of F8-08 (The UCX project, UCX documentation); R2 of F8-08 (ompi_info and the UCX module folder on this build (ompi_build.log); package versions from the system's package list (UCX 1.16.0)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a standard set of small MPI test programs that measure latency and bandwidth between ranks.
analogy: timing a test parcel of each size between two halls.
precise: a benchmark suite from Ohio State University (curriculum reading-list item 83) whose point-to-point and collective tests can place buffers in host or device memory; milestone F4 asks for their device-buffer results "logged next to host-buffer results".
source: D3 of F8-08 (The Ohio State University, OSU Micro-Benchmarks documentation); C1 of F8-08 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14.1 rows "MPI with GPUs" and "GPUDirect", and section 14.3 milestone F4 (goal, build, acceptance tests quoted verbatim); a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: moving a big GPU buffer through host memory in pieces, so the copy of one piece overlaps the network transfer of the previous one.
analogy: a bucket chain: while one crate is on the road, the next is being carried to the dock.
precise: splitting a message into chunks and running the three stages (device-to-host copy, network transfer, host-to-device copy) concurrently on different chunks; for k chunks the time is about the first chunk's three stages plus (k − 1) times the slowest stage.
source: D4 of F8-09 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series, and the UCX documentation); R6 of F8-09 (run of Listing 4 (two_node_model.log, input two_node_model.in, invented TN-2 parameters), g++ 13.3.0 with sanitizers, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of Open MPI that actually moves bytes over one kind of path: shared memory, TCP, or a network card.
analogy: the kind of vehicle a parcel travels in: corridor trolley, road van, courier.
precise: an Open MPI component framework whose components (this build lists ofi, openib, tcp, vader, self) are selected per peer at start-up; the verbose log reports the choice as "Using <name> btl for send to …". Open MPI can instead use UCX through a different layer for the same job.
source: D4 of F8-09 (The Open MPI Project, Open MPI documentation for the 4.1 series, and the UCX documentation); R3 of F8-09 (transport log of the default run (transport_shm.log), --mca btl_base_verbose 30, filtered and sorted; the component list (btl: ofi, openib, tcp, vader, self) is from ompi_info on the same machine) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an all-reduce done in levels: first inside each machine, then between machines, then inside each machine again.
analogy: each building totals its own soup into quarters, matching halls in different buildings trade quarters by road, then each building shares the finished quarters.
precise: an all-reduce over P = N × G ranks composed of a reduce-scatter on each node's communicator, an all-reduce of each shard on the communicator of ranks with the same local rank (one per node), and an all-gather on each node's communicator; the network then carries 2(N − 1)/N · S bytes per node instead of the flat ring's 2(P − 1)/P · S per network crossing.
source: D2 of F8-10 (R. Thakur, R. Rabenseifner, W. Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH"); R3 of F8-10 (run of Listing 2 (hier_model.log, input hier_model.in, invented TN-2 parameters), g++ 13.3.0 with sanitizers, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a process's number among the processes on its own machine.
analogy: the station number of a hall inside its building; every building has a station 1.
precise: the rank of a process in a communicator that contains only the processes of its node; in MPI it is obtained by splitting MPI_COMM_WORLD by node (with MPI_Comm_split_type(…, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, …) on real nodes) and calling MPI_Comm_rank on the result.
source: D1 of F8-10 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: making smaller groups out of a big group of processes, each group with its own numbering.
analogy: the delivery service drawing up a separate phone list per building, and another per station number.
precise: MPI_Comm_split(comm, color, key, &newcomm) is collective over comm; processes passing the same color end up in the same new communicator, ordered by key. Listing 1 calls it twice: color = node gives the node communicator, color = local rank gives the cross-node communicator.
source: D1 of F8-10 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the order in which numbers are added; with floating-point numbers, a different order can give a slightly different answer.
analogy: pouring the same soups into the pot in a different order and getting a pot that weighs a few grains different.
precise: floating-point addition is not associative, so two correct all-reduce algorithms that combine contributions in different orders can produce results differing in the last bits; a collective is reproducible if it returns bit-identical results for identical inputs and process layout, which some libraries offer as an option at a cost in speed.
source: R1 of F8-10 (run of Listing 1, checked, on 4, 8, 8 and 6 ranks (hier_ok.log), Open MPI 4.1.6 with g++ 13.3.0, one shared container, exit code 0); R4 of F8-10 (ompi_info on the same machine (han_info.log): coll components and the coll_han_priority and coll_han_reproducible parameters with their help text, exit code 0)

simple: moving data at the same time as calculating, so the total time is less than the two added up.
analogy: the van drives across town while the kitchen cooks the next course.
precise: running communication operations concurrently with computation that does not depend on them, so that step time approaches max(compute, communication) rather than their sum; it needs independent work, hardware that can do both at once, and a software path that lets the communication advance while the computation runs.
source: D2 of F8-11 (S. Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training"); C1 of F8-11 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14.3 milestone F6 (goal, reading, build and acceptance test quoted verbatim) and F3; a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a group operation that you start with one call and finish with another, with other work in between.
analogy: handing the crate to the depot and getting a ticket; you collect the result later with the ticket.
precise: MPI's MPI_I… collectives (here MPI_Iallreduce) return a request immediately; the operation is complete only after a successful MPI_Test… or MPI_Wait… on it, and the buffer must not be touched until then; all ranks must start collectives on a communicator in the same order.
source: D1 of F8-11 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the library actually doing the steps of an operation you have started.
analogy: someone has to go out and wave the van on.
precise: the execution of the internal steps (sends, receives, reductions) of pending non-blocking operations; depending on the library, transport and configuration, it happens only inside MPI calls on the calling thread, or also in a progress thread or in network hardware. Listing 1's notest schedule shows a case where it happened only in the final wait (R1).
source: D1 of F8-11 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard"); R1 of F8-11 (run of Listing 1 on 2 processes (overlap_mpi.log), Open MPI 4.1.6 with g++ 13.3.0, one shared 4-CPU container, exit code 0; measured on this container (AH-23)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the communication time that the computation does not cover, so it adds to the step time.
analogy: the time the kitchen stands idle waiting for the last van.
precise: step time minus the time of the computation the communication could have overlapped (here the backward pass); hidden communication is total communication minus exposed communication. Listing 3 prints both.
source: R3 of F8-11 (run of Listing 3 (timeline_model.log, input timeline_model.in, invented TN-2 values), g++ 13.3.0 with sanitizers, exit code 0)
